correctness.rationale: For θ>0, differentiation of the known copula gives the two conditional CDFs. Integrating their squares over the correct piecewise domains yields ξ(V|U)=2θ²/[(1+θ)(1+2θ)] and ξ(U|V)=2θ/(3+2θ). Their subtraction is strictly positive. Differentiating the exact gap reduces the global maximum to the unique positive zero of 8θ³+12θ²−3, whose monotonicity proves uniqueness and globality. Symbolic integration and separate direct conditional-CDF adaptive quadratures checked all displayed identities and five parameter values; numerical tests are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The asymmetry of a negative-dependence model creates a natural open question: which of two uniformized coordinates is more predictable from the other? The previous symmetric Kendall and Spearman correlations erase this orientation, whereas Chatterjee ξ is intrinsically directional. Explicit full-domain formulas and an exact attained maximum of the predictive asymmetry provide model-specific information useful for dependence assessment; it is not a routine numerical table or arbitrary parameter slice.
